title: Keynote: Can you trust your (large language) model? - Jodie Burchell - NDC AI 2025

segments.text: So, good morning everyone and welcome to
the very first NDC AAI. How are we all
feeling today? We excited to be here?
Yes. Yes. I am very excited to be here
today and I'm very excited to be
speaking about a topic that is very near
and dear to my heart and that's the
topic of whether you can trust your
models. So, I've worked as a data
scientist for many years now, and this
is a to a topic that I have had to
tackle many times throughout my career,
and it's not an easy question often to
answer. And it's even harder now because
we've moved into the age of gigantic
complex blackbox LLMs.
But of course, we are talking about data
science. We are obviously talking about
something much more scientific than the
idea of blind trust. We're in fact
talking about the question of whether
you have measured things properly. And
to illustrate the difference between
trusting your results and actually
measuring them correctly, I'm going to
start by telling you a story.
So back in 2010, a social psychologist
called Amy Cuddi was teaching at Harvard
Business School and she started noticing
a difference between her group of
students. This is always the problem
when you study undergraduate psychology.
Your professors start experimenting on
you. So she had two types of students in
her classes. She had one group that was
doing very well at written assessment,
but when it came to class participation,
they were very reluctant. They would
half raise their hands almost as though
they were protecting themselves and when
they were called upon to speak they were
very reluctant. They lacked conviction
in what they said. But then you had
another group of students. The students
were doing very well at written
assessment but they were also very keen
to do class participation. So they would
raise their hands high and they would
have a huge amount of confidence when
they spoke.
So, Cardi got to wondering, could there
be a relationship between confidence and
body language that went both ways? That
is, by having more confident body
language, could you actually become more
confident? So, this kicked off Cuddy's
research into what she called power
posing. And what she did is she got a
group of participants and got them to do
some sort of difficult, intimidating

groups. And one group, she got them to
hold these sort of expansive high power
poses like this one, the Wonder Woman
pose. And she found that this group
actually were more confident at doing
this task. They reported feeling more
confident. They reported more feelings

actually showed physiological changes

levels of testosterone and lower levels
of cortisol. So they actually were
feeling more dominant and less stressed.
So these were exciting findings and
these actually really impressed the
scientific community. Cuddi ended up
with a publication in the top journal in
psychology
and then her findings hit the

So people everywhere were going into

posing had become a phenomenon.
That was until 2014.

almost identical scans in the same

things have gotten really difficult as

learned from the data. There is actually

So, it brings us back to the question I

Well, if you've been a person existing

So what does it mean when an LLM

Well, it comes down to how and why we
